elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered retains automatic renewal ("This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date") and no mutual-written-agreement gate was added; the conditional automatic-renewal elements below (30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder) are not all met, so the mutual-agreement default is not excused.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — 12-month renewal terms, unchanged by the redline and already compliant.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered language sets the exit at "written notice to the other at least sixty (60) days in advance" — 60 days, which exceeds the preferred 30-day opt-out ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered Section 4.1; the 60-day reminder is only mentioned aspirationally in the margin comment ("we would prefer 30 days with a 60-day renewal reminder"), which is not operative language.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the only pricing term, Section 3.1, is a fixed revenue share ("thirty percent ... of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month") with no renewal uplift or repricing right anywhere in the cited text, so no price-increase cap is triggered.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Operative text now reads "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon written notice to the other at least sixty (60) days in advance," replacing the original "ninety (90) days written notice" — a 60-day window, exactly at the fallback ceiling. The failing deterministic check ("number not found") is a false negative caused by the reordered phrasing (notice first, period after) rather than an absent number; the substance is compliant.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: fees are fixed at 30% of Net Sales above the $11,000 monthly threshold under Section 3.1 and the Agreement confers no renewal price-uplift right, so no 5% cap is required. (The mapping's "already_met" quote of Section 3.1 is better characterised as condition-not-triggered, but the outcome is the same.)

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the notice window is reset to sixty (60) days in operative text and the price-cap element is untriggered because Section 3.1 fixes consideration as a 30% Net Sales share with no renewal uplift mechanic.

Preferred level fails on three elements: renewal remains automatic without a mutual-written-agreement gate, the opt-out is 60 rather than ≤30 days, and no 60-day Vendor renewal reminder was inserted (it appears only in the margin comment). To reach preferred, the drafter would need operative text setting the opt-out at thirty (30) days and adding an affirmative HDI obligation to notify the Company at least sixty (60) days before each renewal date.

The deterministic check "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days" reports "number not found," but inspection of the substance shows the regex simply did not match the reordered construction "written notice to the other at least sixty (60) days in advance." The 60-day figure is present and unambiguous, so this failure should not block the fallback.

Minimal: the edit touches only the notice period inside the existing single sentence, leaves the one-year renewal term, the mutual either-Party structure, the Effective Date mechanics and the "Termination Date" definition intact, and adds no survival tail, reminder procedure, uplift cap or other extra beyond the fallback checklist.

Intent preserved: no undefined terms or dangling cross-references result; "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the 'Termination Date')" still reads correctly against the amended sentence.

Non-blocking caution for the drafter: because Section 4.1 is mutual, shortening 90 days to 60 days also shortens the notice HDI must give the Company for a convenience exit. If continuity of hosting matters commercially, consider a split construction (Company non-renewal on sixty (60) days; HDI on not less than ninety (90) days) — but note that adding the split would exceed the fallback checklist and should be raised in negotiation rather than as part of this minimal redline.

Deviation classification is correct: the original 90-day window exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling on a material term but is not itself walk-away (windows must be longer than 90 days, or renewals multi-year, to be walk-away).
